questions.prompt: Because he hated the tyrant, the citizen fled from the city.
questions.answer: Quod tyrannum ōderat, cīvis ex cīvitāte effūgit.

questions.prompt: I remember the letter which the soldier had sent.
questions.answer: Meminī epistolam quam mīles mīserat.

questions.prompt: The wolf began to be feared by the shepherds.
questions.answer: Lupus ā pāstōribus timērī coeptus est.

questions.prompt: The queen hates those who despise the ancient laws.
questions.answer: Rēgīna ōdit eōs quī antīquās lēgēs contemnunt.

questions.prompt: You remember the words of the poet whom we admired.
questions.answer: Meministī verba poētae quem mīrātī sumus.

questions.prompt: Having captured the town, the general began to divide the spoils.
questions.answer: Oppidō captō, dux praedam dīvidere coepit.

questions.prompt: I shall hate that man forever, because he betrayed his country.
questions.answer: Illum in perpetuum ōderō, quod patriam prōdidit.

questions.prompt: The girl began to weep when she saw the broken statue.
questions.answer: Puella flēre coepit cum statuam frāctam vīdit.

questions.prompt: We remember the brave men who died for the republic.
questions.answer: Meminimus virōrum fortium quī prō rē pūblicā periērunt.

questions.prompt: Remember, soldiers, the glory of your ancestors!
questions.answer: Mementōte, mīlitēs, glōriae māiōrum vestrōrum!

questions.prompt: The old man remembered the war which he had waged in his youth.
questions.answer: Senex meminerat bellī quod in iuventūte gesserat.

questions.prompt: Although they hated the king, they obeyed his commands.
questions.answer: Quamquam rēgem ōderant, imperiīs eius pāruērunt.

questions.prompt: The hind, terrified by the wolf, began to flee through the woods.
questions.answer: Cerva lupō territa per silvās fugere coepit.

questions.prompt: If you had remembered my advice, you would not have erred.
questions.answer: Sī cōnsilī meī meminissēs, nōn errāvissēs.

questions.prompt: The enemy, having been conquered, began to be scattered across the fields.
questions.answer: Hostēs victī per agrōs spargī coeptī sunt.

questions.prompt: I hate the man who often deceives his friends with lies.
questions.answer: Ōdī hominem quī saepe mendāciīs amīcōs dēcipit.

questions.prompt: Once the storm had begun, the fishermen feared for their lives.
questions.answer: Ubi tempestās coeperat, piscātōrēs dē vītā timuērunt.

questions.prompt: Remember that all men are going to die.
questions.answer: Mementō omnēs hominēs moritūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: When the consul had begun to speak, the crowd fell silent.
questions.answer: Cum cōnsul dīcere coepisset, turba conticuit.

questions.prompt: We shall remember this day as long as we live.
questions.answer: Huius diēī meminerimus dum vīvēmus.

questions.prompt: The gods hate the proud, but they love the humble.
questions.answer: Deī superbōs ōdērunt, sed humilēs amant.

questions.prompt: Having read the letter, the maiden began to hope again.
questions.answer: Epistolā lēctā, virgō rūrsus spērāre coepit.

questions.prompt: The general, having pitched camp, began to fortify the walls with great care.
questions.answer: Dux, castrīs positīs, magnā cūrā mūrōs mūnīre coepit.

questions.prompt: We hate the arrogant judge who condemns the innocent for money.
questions.answer: Ōdimus superbum iūdicem quī innocentēs pecūniā damnat.

questions.prompt: Remember, my son, the promises which you made to your father.
questions.answer: Mementō, fīlī mī, prōmissa quae patrī tuō fēcistī.

questions.prompt: After the wall had begun to be built, the enemy attacked the city.
questions.answer: Postquam mūrus aedificārī coeptus est, hostēs urbem oppugnāvērunt.

questions.prompt: I shall hate the traitors as long as I live, because they surrendered the citadel.
questions.answer: Ōderō prōditōrēs dum vīvam, quod arcem trādidērunt.

questions.prompt: The old woman still remembers the songs which the shepherds used to sing.
questions.answer: Anus etiam meminit carmina quae pāstōrēs canere solēbant.

questions.prompt: When spring had come, the birds began to build their nests in the tall trees.
questions.answer: Cum vēr vēnisset, avēs in altīs arboribus nīdōs facere coepērunt.

questions.prompt: Although he hated war, the wise king remembered the fallen soldiers with tears.
questions.answer: Quamquam bellum ōderat, rēx sapiēns mīlitēs cāsōs cum lacrimīs meminerat.
